title: K-flat scalar cone and its natural total-tensor model
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a closed braided monoidal Grothendieck abelian category with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian, def-sfb-monoidal-category, lem-sfb-derived-monoidal]. Let $B$ be a commutative ring acting linearly on $\mathcal A$, with $(b u)\otimes v=b(u\otimes v)=u\otimes(b v)$ for morphisms $u,v$ and $b\in B$. Fix $b\in B$, and put
$$P_b=\operatorname{Cone}(b:\mathbf1[0]\to\mathbf1[0]),$$
with the cochain and cone conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $P_b$ is K-flat for the total tensor product and two-sided quasi-isomorphism convention of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. For every unbounded cochain complex $C$ there is an isomorphism of complexes
$$\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes P_b)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(b:C\to C),$$
natural in chain maps $C\to C'$. If $Q$ is cochain localization, its composite with the canonical K-flat tensor comparison gives isomorphisms
$$QC\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP_b\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\operatorname{Cone}(b:C\to C),$$
natural in $C$. Thus the displayed cochain cone functor inverts quasi-isomorphisms after localization and descends with these isomorphisms to a functor naturally isomorphic to $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP_b$ on $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: DerivedCategory.kFlat_scalarCone (lines 67-76), isIso_μ_scalarCone (79-88), tensorScalarConeIso' (103-116), tensorScalarConeIso'_hom_naturality (120-134), tensorScalarConeIso (147-149), and tensorScalarConeIso_hom_naturality (152-158); binder context at 37-42.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-unit-endomorphism-cone-coordinates] with $a=b1_{\mathbf1}$. The assumed tensor linearity and linearity of the unitors give $a^R_C=a^L_C=b1_C$. Its signed chain maps therefore give $\Phi_C:\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes P_b)\cong F_b(C)=\operatorname{Cone}(b1_C)$ and the left-tensor analogue. Its diagonal naturality equations assemble $\Phi$ as a natural isomorphism; the identity and composition laws of the diagonal cone maps are componentwise.

source.place: On X, tensoring the two-term resolution gives the cone naturally.

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism $f:C\to C\prime$, scalar linearity gives $f(b1_C)=(b1_{C\prime})f$. Apply [lem-pe-cone-square-quasi-isomorphism] with $s=t=f$. Thus $F_b(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Conjugating it by the two natural chain isomorphisms of step 1 proves that both $\operatorname{Tot}(f\otimes1_{P_b})$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(1_{P_b}\otimes f)$ are quasi-isomorphisms: their cohomology maps are conjugates of isomorphisms. These are exactly the two requirements for K-flatness in [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso].

source.place: On X, hence K-flat; cone calculation and invariance.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal], the derived tensor is computed by replacing either argument by a K-flat resolution. Use the identity resolution of $P_b$ from step 2. Hence the canonical lax tensor comparison $\mu_{C,P_b}:QC\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP_b\to Q\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes P_b)$ is invertible. Define $\theta_C=Q(\Phi_C)\circ\mu_{C,P_b}$. Naturality of the comparison and of $\Phi$ makes $\theta$ a natural isomorphism, with precisely the required comparison formula.

source.place: On X, resolution computes the derived tensor and the natural cone identification.

proof.text: Step 2 and localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] show $QF_b$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms. The localization property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives a descended functor and lifts $\theta$ to its natural isomorphism with derived right tensor. Concretely choose the descended functor to be $T=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP_b$, its comparison $TQ\cong QF_b$ to be $\theta$, and its comparison with derived right tensor to be $1_T$. The compatibility equation is then $\theta_C\circ1=\theta_C$.

source.place: On X, naturality in K after derived localization.
